title: Dad-Dont-Worry-WEZZA-c16e5767-v2
style: Acoustic hip-hop with a folk-influenced arrangement. Features a fingerpicked acoustic guitar playing a repetitive minor-key progression, a clean electric bass, and a steady boom-bap drum pattern with a crisp snare and dry kick. Male vocals are delivered in a rhythmic, melodic rap style with occasional layered harmonies. The tempo is 88 BPM in 4/4 time. The arrangement is sparse, focusing on the interplay between the syncopated guitar melody and the vocal delivery. Subtle atmospheric synth pads appear in the background during the chorus sections. The track maintains a consistent dynamic level throughout.
lyrics:
[Intro]
[fingerpicked acoustic guitar, clean electric bass]

[Verse 1]
[melodic male rap vocals]
Wes said, "Dad, don't worry, no one's coming here."
I thought I was the one on watch, turns out he is too.
Nine years old, teaching his old man a steady view.
Kid looked at me, calm, didn't even flinch, said, "Dad, don't worry, no one's coming here."
And he's right, no one's coming here, because we built a house that nobody dares.
Still, we stay ready anyway, right Wes? "Yeah, Dad, I got my plan too."
Gaming PC, general, nine-year-old planner, already mapped the paths, already thought through.

[Chorus]
[drum beat enters, boom-bap style]
Dad, don't worry, no one's coming here.
Dad, don't worry, Wes is on the watch.
Four homes for one troop, redundancy set.
Father and son, both the calm, both the catch.
Dad, don't worry, we're ready anyway.
Dad, don't worry, we don't sleep dumb.
Stay prepared is the rule we ride, that's the family pulse from me to my son.

[Verse 2]
[drums continue, bass locks with kick]
Wasn't meant to be the kid reassuring me, was supposed to flow the other way, supposed to be the rule.
But he looked at me steady and I heard the father's tone coming out of the son's mouth, same shade, different tool.
That's when I knew the doctrine had landed, that's when I knew the teaching had held.
He's not worried because I'm not worried, and I'm not worried because the stack won't bell.
You want to know why I don't carry fear? [guitar continues arpeggio]
Because I already did the care.
Four homes, one truth, one son who gets it.
Nine years old, holding the line with his father.

[Chorus]
[layered vocal harmonies enter]
Dad, don't worry, no one's coming here.
Dad, don't worry, Wes is on the watch.
Four homes for one troop, redundancy set.
Father and son, both the calm, both the catch.
Dad, don't worry, we're ready anyway.
Dad, don't worry, we don't sleep dumb.
Stay prepared is the rule we ride, that's the family pulse from me to my son.

[Outro]
[drums drop out, acoustic guitar only]
Wes said it first, I'm just echoing back the truth.
Corey, 036.
[vocalizing] La la la la...
[guitar fades out]
